answer: At a lake oasis, delivery agents verify water drums unloaded at a jetty. Each drum has a one-use seal with jade dye, and two independent scales sign its weight at loading and receipt. The exchange pays one bounty per sealed drum only after the readings match; aliases filing the same receipt split that single payment. A sybil operator needs additional real deliveries, valid seals, and a bond at risk for every claim, so extra accounts alone earn nothing. Stolen seals and colluding scale operators remain possible; random manual checks and public weight logs limit that weakness.
